todos.description: Display the tags on the photo
todos.context: The center panel is a zoomable image widget (ui.Viewer, wrapped by MainWindow into a Border with the ActionPanel on top and stacked with the grid viewer), and today nothing is painted over the photo: per the standing UI Layout decision in CLAUDE.md, favorite/color state is surfaced only through the toolbar buttons, the context menu and the file list, all driven from Application.showPhoto -> updateActionStates. Tags (title + keywords) are visible only inside the modal Tags dialog, which re-reads them per photo through exifService.GetStockInfo from the XMP sidecar/JPEG packet; there is no in-memory tag cache yet (todo #1). Where the tags go relative to the "nothing over the photo" rule is not decided yet.

plan.summary: Surface the current photo's stock tags (title + keywords) in the center panel without breaking the standing "nothing is drawn over the photo" rule: add a new `ui.TagBar` strip that MainWindow places in the bottom slot of the center Border (below the zoomable viewer), fed from `Application.showPhoto` by an asynchronous, debounced `exifService.GetStockInfo` read that is applied only while the photo it was started for is still the current one. The bar collapses to zero height when the photo has no tags, is suppressed in grid mode, stays in sync with edits made in the Tags dialog (generate / save / close), and can be toggled off with a new `I` shortcut whose state is remembered in preferences. No core package changes are needed: `GetStockInfo` already returns exactly the data required and is safe to call from a worker goroutine (it takes the service RLock); every widget touch is wrapped in `fyne.Do` per the project's threading rules. The work is independent of todo #1 (the tag cache), which would later only replace the read behind `loadTagsFor` with a cache lookup.

steps.title: Add the TagBar widget
steps.details: New `ui.TagBar` in `internal/gui/ui/tagbar.go`, modelled on the small composite widgets already in the package (Notifier, ActionPanel): `NewTagBar() *TagBar`, `Container() *fyne.Container`, `SetTags(model.Tags)`, `Clear()`, `SetEnabled(bool)` (user toggle) and `SetSuppressed(bool)` (grid mode). Internals: a padded VBox with a bold title `widget.Label` and a keywords `widget.Label`, both `Truncation = fyne.TextTruncateEllipsis` so the strip keeps a fixed two-line height whatever the tags are; keywords rendered via `model.Tags.KeywordLine()`. Visibility is derived, not set directly: the container shows only when `enabled && !suppressed && !tags.IsEmpty()`; a single `refresh()` recomputes it after every setter. Empty title or empty keyword list hides just that label. Tests in `internal/gui/ui/tagbar_test.go` following `tags_dialog_test.go` (fyne `test.NewTempWindow`, testify, non-parallel): tags shown, empty tags hide the bar, `Clear` hides it, disabled bar stays hidden after `SetTags`, re-enabling brings it back, suppression wins over enabled.

steps.title: Place the bar under the photo in MainWindow
steps.details: Extend `NewMainWindow` with a `*TagBar` parameter, store it on `MainWindow`, and in `build()` change the center panel to `container.NewBorder(mw.actionPanel.Container(), mw.tagBar.Container(), nil, nil, mw.viewStack)` so the strip sits below the viewer and never overlaps the image (the notifier stack stays as it is). In `SetGridMode` call `mw.tagBar.SetSuppressed(grid)` next to the existing action panel show/hide. Add thin forwarders used by the app layer: `SetPhotoTags(model.Tags)`, `ClearPhotoTags()`, `SetTagsVisible(bool)`. Update the single construction site in `internal/gui/app/app.go` (`ui.NewTagBar()` built next to `ui.NewNotifier()` and passed in).

steps.title: Load and show the tags of the current photo
steps.details: New `internal/gui/app/tags_view.go` holding the read path. `Application` gains two fields (`tagGeneration int`, `tagTimer *time.Timer`). `showTagsFor(photo model.Photo)`: increments the generation, clears the bar immediately (the strip must never describe the previous photo, same reasoning as `clearActionStates`), stops any pending timer and starts `time.AfterFunc(tagReadDelay, ...)` with ~200ms so arrow-key scrolling does not open every skipped JPEG; the timer goroutine calls `a.exifService.GetStockInfo(photo)` and then `fyne.Do` to check `a.tagGeneration == captured` plus `navigator.Current().ImagePath == photo.ImagePath` before `a.mainWindow.SetPhotoTags(info.Tags)` (stale results dropped, read errors only logged). `clearTags()` bumps the generation, stops the timer and clears the bar. Call `showTagsFor` from `Application.showPhoto` in `internal/gui/app/navigation.go` (both on the success and the load-failure branch, next to `updateActionStates`) and `clearTags` from `clearViewer` in `internal/gui/app/actions.go`. Grid mode needs nothing extra.

steps.title: Keep the bar in sync with the Tags dialog
steps.details: In `internal/gui/app/actions.go` push the dialog's tags into the bar instead of re-reading the file: add `setTagsIfCurrent(photo model.Photo, tags model.Tags)` to `internal/gui/app/tags_view.go` (bumps the generation so an in-flight read cannot overwrite the newer tags, then sets the bar only while `navigator.Current()` is still that photo) and call it from `tagsSession.generate` right after `s.dialog.SetTags(generated)`, from `tagsSession.saveJPEG`/`saveSidecar` success and from `tagsSession.close` after the final `saveSidecar`, so an edit made in the dialog — including clearing both fields — is visible under the photo the moment the dialog goes away. `prefill` also calls it, which gives the bar the freshly read tags when the dialog was opened before the debounced read finished.

steps.title: Toggle shortcut, help entry and documentation
steps.details: Add `OnToggleTags` to `ui.ShortcutCallbacks` and bind it to `glfw.KeyI` in the scancode map in `internal/gui/ui/shortcuts.go` (I is free: F R G B D C N S 1-4 H Y L Z T are taken). Wire it in `internal/gui/app/app.go` to a handler in `internal/gui/app/tags_view.go` that flips `a.showTags`, calls `a.mainWindow.SetTagsVisible(...)` and persists the flag; guard it with the existing `shortcutsBlocked()`. Persist through `internal/gui/app/settings.go` with a `showTagsKey = "showTags"` constant, restored by a new `restoreTagVisibility` called from `Run` before the first directory load, default true. Add `{"I", "Toggle tag strip"}` to `helpLeft` in `internal/gui/ui/help.go`. Update `CLAUDE.md`: the UI Layout section gets a line saying the tag strip sits below the photo (the favorite/color rule is unchanged), and the Keyboard Shortcuts list gets `I`.

questions.question: Placement: assume a strip below the photo (inside the center panel, image never covered) unless you want the tags painted over the bottom of the image the way the notifier toast is — which would need the CLAUDE.md 'nothing is drawn over the photo' rule amended. Affects steps 1-2.

Content: assume one truncated line for the title and one truncated line for the keywords (fixed height, full text stays in the Tags dialog). Do you instead want the keywords word-wrapped over several lines, or the keyword count only? Affects step 1.
Toggle: assume the strip can be hidden with `I` and that the choice is remembered between launches, default on. Is `I` acceptable, or should the strip always be on? Affects step 5.
Photos with no tags: assume the strip collapses completely (no 'no tags' placeholder), so the viewer keeps the full height for untagged folders. Affects step 1.
Read cost: assume a ~200ms debounce before reading tags during navigation, and that a read error is only logged, not shown as an error toast. Affects step 3.

risks: Every navigation step reads the XMP/EXIF of a file until todo #1 lands a tag cache; the debounce limits it, but a slow network volume can still make the strip lag behind the photo.

The strip appearing and disappearing changes the viewer's height, so a zoomed-in photo is re-laid out (pan is clamped in `zoomWidget.clampPan`, so nothing breaks, but the view shifts). Fixed strip height keeps the shift constant.
`NewMainWindow`'s signature changes; it has one caller (`internal/gui/app/app.go`) but is already six parameters long and grows to seven.
Stale-result handling depends on the generation counter plus the current-path check; getting either wrong shows one photo's tags under another.
`GetStockInfo` returns empty tags and no error for a PNG or a JPEG without EXIF, which is indistinguishable from 'no tags' — acceptable, but it means the strip cannot report an unreadable file.

todos.description: Add a background mode for tag generation
todos.context: Tag generation (stock title + keywords via the claude CLI in internal/core/tags) runs only as a foreground, per-photo modal flow today: `T` -> Application.handleTags builds a tagsSession whose generate() spawns a goroutine writing into the Tags dialog and an XMP sidecar, with the context cancelled in tagsSession.close when the dialog is dismissed. Existing background machinery it would sit next to: imaging.Provider.LoadFolder (bounded worker pool, generation counters, onLoaded callback), the bulk-operation pattern in handleCopyAll/handleDeleteAll with ui.BulkDialog progress, and ui.Notifier for completion messages; the Fyne threading rules in CLAUDE.md apply to any UI update from a worker goroutine. Related open todos: #1 tag cache, #2 display tags on the photo.

plan.summary: Add background (non-modal) tag generation alongside today's per-photo modal flow. A new core `tags.Queue` runs Claude CLI requests on a bounded worker pool with cancellation, de-duplication and progress/result callbacks, mirroring the shape of imaging.Provider.LoadFolder. A new GUI-side controller (internal/gui/app/tags_background.go) owns that queue, applies the persistence policy (XMP sidecar next to the RAW), reports progress and reports the summary through ui.Notifier, always hopping to fyne.Do before touching widgets. Two entry points use it: a new "Tag All" button in the file browser bulk bar that tags the currently filtered photos, and the existing Tags dialog, whose in-flight run is handed over to the controller instead of being cancelled when the dialog is dismissed. A small progress row with a Stop button in the left panel shows how far the batch is and cancels it. Help text is updated last.

steps.title: Add a bounded tag-generation queue to internal/core/tags
steps.details: New file internal/core/tags/queue.go with a `Queue` that has no Fyne and no I/O beyond the generator it is given: `NewQueue(generate func(context.Context, Request) (model.Tags, error), workers int) *Queue`, so *Tagger is passed as `tagger.Generate` and tests inject a fake. State under one mutex: pending []Request, active map keyed by Request.Photo.ImagePath (re-enqueueing a queued or running photo is a no-op), running worker count, done/total counters for the current burst, and a ctx/cancel created when the first worker starts. API: `Enqueue(reqs ...Request) int`, `Cancel()`, `Progress() (done, total int)`, `Busy() bool`, and a `Callbacks` struct with `OnResult(Result)` and `OnFinished(Summary)`. Each worker pops under the lock, runs generate with the queue context, fires OnResult, and the last worker fires OnFinished exactly once. Comment that callbacks run on worker goroutines (the CLAUDE.md fyne.Do rule then applies to callers). Also add `var ErrUsageLimit = errors.New("usage limit reached")` in internal/core/tags/tagger.go, wrapped into the usage-limit branch of responseMessage/responseFailure with %w (message text unchanged), so a batch can stop itself. Tests in internal/core/tags/queue_test.go (table/subtest style like tagger_test.go, testify): concurrency never exceeds `workers`, duplicates dropped, Cancel stops pending work and cancels the passed context, OnFinished fires once with the right counts, per-photo results and errors. Extend tagger_test.go with an errors.Is(err, ErrUsageLimit) assertion on the existing usage-limit fixtures.

steps.title: Add the GUI-side background tagging controller and wire it into Application
steps.details: New file internal/gui/app/tags_background.go holding `backgroundTagger`: it owns a *tags.Queue built over a.tagger.Generate plus the policy the queue must not know about. The `generate` wrapper calls a.tagger.Generate and on success persists: when photo.HasRAW(), imaging.WriteSidecar(model.SidecarPath(photo.RAWPath), tags), mirroring tagsSession.saveSidecar; a photo without a RAW pair is not written to at all and is counted as skipped. `RunNow(req, onResult)` starts a single detached goroutine outside the pool for the Tags dialog (step 4) so an interactive run is never stuck behind a batch, sharing the same persist + notify path. Failures are logged (log.Printf, as handleDeleteAll does); a tags.ErrUsageLimit result cancels the whole batch and shows one warning. Every UI touch goes through fyne.Do because callbacks arrive on queue workers. Wire it in internal/gui/app/app.go: new field `bgTags *backgroundTagger`, constructed in New() (`backgroundTagWorkers = 2`) and given its window/progress hooks in Run() after mainWindow exists; cancel the queue from the window's close/lifecycle hook next to the existing SetOnStarted wiring. Inert but compiles and is reviewable on its own.

steps.title: Add the "Tag All" bulk entry point over the filtered photos
steps.details: internal/gui/ui/filebrowser.go: add `OnTagAll func()` to FileBrowserCallbacks and a `tagAllBtn` (theme.DocumentCreateIcon(), the icon the Tags action uses in toolbar.go) into fb.bulkBar next to Delete All / Copy All, under the same visibility rule (updateBulkBarVisibility). internal/gui/ui/bulk_dialog.go: add `NewTagAllDialogContent(count int) (*fyne.Container, *widget.Check)` following NewDeleteAllDialogContent — a bold "Generate tags for N filtered photos?" label plus a "Skip photos that already have tags" check (checked by default), wrapped in minWidthLayout{width: copyDialogWidth}. internal/gui/app/actions.go: `handleTagAll` next to handleDeleteAll/handleCopyAll — guard on a.gridMode || a.dialogs.anyOpen(), take a.fileBrowser.FilteredPhotos(), show the confirm dialog through a.dialogs.open(dialogTagAll, ...), and on confirm start one goroutine that (a) with the skip box checked drops photos whose exifService.GetStockInfo already returns non-empty tags, (b) builds tags.Request values with the stored `claudePath` preference and no notes, (c) enqueues them via a.bgTags and reports "Queued N photos for tagging" (or "Nothing to tag") through fyne.Do + ShowNotification. internal/gui/app/dialogs.go: add the `dialogTagAll` kind. internal/gui/app/app.go: pass OnTagAll: a.handleTagAll in the FileBrowserCallbacks literal.

steps.title: Let a Tags dialog run survive the dialog being closed
steps.details: internal/gui/app/actions.go: route tagsSession.generate through a.bgTags.RunNow instead of its own goroutine + tagger call. The result callback keeps the existing `a.dialogs.isCurrent(s.dialog)` guard, keeps setting the `claudePath` preference on success, and keeps calling s.dialog.SetTags / s.dialog.Fail; the sidecar write for generated tags now belongs to the controller alone, so tagsSession.saveSidecar keeps only its close-time job of persisting user edits (leave its `saved` bookkeeping intact so a run followed by a close does not write the same bytes twice — WriteSidecar already no-ops on identical content). Stop cancelling the run in tagsSession.close: drop the per-session context and the cancel passed to a.dialogs.open, so `Esc` or Close leaves the run going; when the run finishes with the dialog gone, the controller persists the sidecar and shows "Tags generated for <name>" (or the failure) through the notifier. Reflect this in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go only if the generating status line should say the run continues in the background (a one-line setStatus text change); extend internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go if that text is asserted.

steps.title: Show background progress with a Stop button in the left panel
steps.details: New internal/gui/ui/tag_progress.go: a small `TagProgress` type wrapping a widget.ProgressBar plus a label ("Tagging 3/20") and a Stop button, hidden by default, with `SetProgress(done, total int)`, `Hide()` and an OnStop callback. internal/gui/ui/filebrowser.go: build one in FileBrowser, add it to the existing `topBars` VBox (below bulkBar so it stays visible whether or not a filter is on), add `OnStopTagging func()` to FileBrowserCallbacks and expose `SetTagProgress(done, total int)` / `HideTagProgress()`. internal/gui/app/tags_background.go: feed OnResult/OnFinished into those two methods inside fyne.Do, and on OnFinished show the summary through the notifier ("Tagged 18/20 photos (2 failed)" as a warning when anything failed or was skipped, a plain notification otherwise), mirroring handleCopyAll's wording. internal/gui/app/app.go: pass OnStopTagging: a.bgTags.Cancel. Add a table test in internal/gui/ui/tag_progress_test.go (test.NewTempWindow like tags_dialog_test.go) covering visibility and label text for zero/partial/complete states.

steps.title: Document the background mode
steps.details: internal/gui/ui/help.go: extend the Actions section only if a keyboard shortcut is added (see the last question); otherwise no change there. CLAUDE.md: in Features/UI Layout, note that Tag All in the bulk bar generates tags for the filtered photos in the background, that background results are written to the XMP sidecar of the RAW pair, that the Tags dialog no longer cancels a run when closed, and that progress is shown in the left panel with a Stop button. Keep the edit confined to the feature/shortcut documentation.

questions.question: Scope check for steps 3 and 4: background mode = (a) bulk tagging of the currently filtered photos plus (b) an interactive run that keeps going after the Tags dialog is closed. Assume both unless told otherwise.

Step 2: how many concurrent claude CLI runs? Each spawns a process with a 3-minute timeout and consumes subscription quota. Assume 2 workers unless told otherwise; should it be a preference instead of a constant?

Step 2: a photo without a RAW pair has nowhere to store tags except the JPEG's own XMP packet, which the foreground flow only writes behind an explicit button. Assume background runs skip JPEG-only photos and count them as skipped, rather than writing into the JPEG.
Step 3: should Tag All skip photos that already carry a title and keywords? Assume yes, with a checkbox in the confirm dialog checked by default.
Step 3: bulk runs send no Concept/Location/Editorial notes, unlike the dialog. Assume no notes unless the dialog's inputs should be reused for the whole batch.
Step 2: should a running batch be cancelled when the user opens another folder or quits? Assume it keeps running across folder changes (paths are absolute) and is cancelled only by Stop or app exit.
Step 2: on a usage-limit error, assume the whole batch is cancelled and one warning is shown, instead of every remaining photo failing the same way.
Step 6: does background tagging need a keyboard shortcut of its own (e.g. Shift+T for the current photo)? Assume no shortcut for now; button only.

risks: Concurrent claude CLI processes multiply cost and can trip the subscription usage limit quickly; the worker count and the usage-limit abort are the only brakes.

Two writers for the same sidecar: the controller writes generated tags while tagsSession still writes edited tags on close. WriteSidecar is a read-modify-write with no lock (ExifService.access does not cover it), so a close landing exactly on a finishing run can lose one of the two writes.

Detaching the dialog run removes the cancel-on-close guarantee: a user who closes the dialog can no longer stop a run except through the new Stop button; make sure the controller's context is also cancelled on app exit so no claude process outlives the window.
Queue callbacks arrive on worker goroutines and the thread checks are compiled out (CLAUDE.md), so a missing fyne.Do will not warn — it will corrupt the canvas intermittently.
Deleting or moving photos while a batch runs leaves stale requests that fail per photo; noise in the summary counts.

Overlap with open todos #1 (tag cache) and #2 (display tags): the persistence helper added here is the code #1 would move behind a cache, so expect a merge touch-up in internal/gui/app/tags_background.go.

todos.context: Codebase-wide simplification pass on a Go + Fyne photo viewer (GUI in internal/gui, everything else in internal/core, which may not import Fyne); a /simplify skill and golangci-lint are configured. The densest spots are internal/gui/app/actions.go (711 lines, 29 funcs, holding button-state sync, per-photo actions, three near-parallel bulk flows handleDeleteAll/handleUnselectAll/handleCopyAll that each repeat the gridMode/dialogs.anyOpen guard plus FilteredPhotos progress-dialog scaffolding, and the whole tagsSession lifecycle) and internal/gui/ui/filebrowser.go (530 lines, 38 funcs mixing tree, list, sorting and color filtering); internal/core/imaging is 22 files whose EXIF/XMP/JPEG-segment responsibilities overlap across exif.go, exif_tags.go, exif_write.go, xmp.go, xmp_packet.go and jpeg_file.go. This is separate work from todo #1 and should not be scoped to the tags change.

plan.summary: A behaviour-neutral simplification pass over the three densest areas of the codebase, done as small independently reviewable steps. In `internal/gui/app` the 768-line `actions.go` is first split by concern (button-state sync, per-photo actions, bulk flows, tags session) with pure code motion, then the repetition inside it is removed: one helper builds and registers every confirm dialog (`handleDelete`, `handleCopy`, `handleDeleteAll`, `handleUnselectAll` all repeat the same six lines), one helper runs a per-photo toggle off the main goroutine (`handleFavorite`/`handleColorToggle`), and the dead `favorite` argument that `handleColorToggle` computes and `photoStateChanged` ignores is removed. In `internal/gui/ui` the 38 `if callbacks.OnX != nil` guards collapse into a `call`/`iconButton` pair, `filebrowser.go` gets one `refreshRows` helper for the applyFilter+bulkbar+Refresh triple it repeats four times, and the row-rendering half of the file moves into its own file with tests. In `internal/core/imaging` two genuine duplications go: the inflight-waiter load dance shared by `Loader.Get` and `Loader.Preload`, and the "read the RAW sidecar and fill what the JPEG lacks" logic that exists in both `ExifService.GetStockInfo` and `Provider.completeStock`. No user-visible behaviour changes anywhere.

steps.title: Split internal/gui/app/actions.go by concern (code motion only)
steps.details: Move code out of `actions.go` into three new files in the same package, changing nothing else, so the diff is reviewable as pure motion. `action_states.go`: `updateActionStates`, `clearActionStates`, `clearViewer`, `favoriteOf`, `metaOf`, `updateFavoriteButtonStates`, `setFavoriteButtonStates`, `updateColorButtonStates`, `handleMetaLoaded`, `photoStateChanged`. `bulk_actions.go`: `handleDeleteAll`, `handleUnselectAll`, `handleCopyAll`. `tags_action.go`: `handleTags`, the whole `tagsSession` type and its methods (`seed`, `storeStock`, `generate`, `saveSidecar`, `saveJPEG`, `close`, `prefill`), the `rewrittenNote` constant and `Application.saveTags`. `actions.go` keeps the per-photo actions and the guards: `handleColorToggle`, `handleFavorite`, `handleCopyToClipboard`, `handleDelete`, `handleCopy`, `handleHelp`, `handleCancel`, `shortcutsBlocked`, `foreignOverlayOnTop`. Fix the import blocks of each file to what it actually uses; keep every comment attached to the function it explains.

steps.title: One confirm-dialog helper and shared guards in internal/gui/app
steps.details: In `dialogs.go` add `func (a *Application) showConfirm(kind dialogKind, title, confirmText, cancelText string, content fyne.CanvasObject, onConfirm func())` that builds `dialog.NewCustomConfirm`, calls `a.dialogs.closed()` and returns early on cancel, registers with `a.dialogs.open(kind, d, nil)` and shows it. Use it in `handleDelete`, `handleCopy` (actions.go) and `handleDeleteAll`, `handleUnselectAll` (bulk_actions.go) — all four register the same way with a nil onCancel today. Add `func (a *Application) dialogBlocked(kind dialogKind) bool` holding the grid-mode / `isOpen(kind)`->`confirm()` / `anyOpen()` triple that `handleDelete` and `handleCopy` repeat; leave `handleHelp` (cancel-on-repeat, no grid guard) and the bulk handlers (`a.gridMode || a.dialogs.anyOpen()`, no confirm-on-repeat — the bulk dialogs have no keyboard shortcut and giving them one would be a behaviour change) as they are. Add `func pathSet(photos []model.Photo) map[string]bool` used by the two places in bulk_actions.go that build that map inline, `func (a *Application) copyPreferences() (string, library.CopyMode)` plus `saveCopyPreferences(dest string, mode library.CopyMode)` used by `handleCopy` and `handleCopyAll`, and `func (a *Application) showErrorAsync(msg string, err error)` wrapping the `fyne.Do(func(){ a.showError(...) })` pattern that appears in the goroutines of `handleColorToggle`, `handleFavorite` and `handleDelete`.

steps.title: Collapse the two per-photo toggles and drop the dead favorite argument
steps.details: `handleFavorite` and `handleColorToggle` differ only in the toggle they call and in whether the app wrote a rating. Add `func (a *Application) toggleCurrentPhoto(failure string, ratingWritten bool, toggle func(model.Photo) (favorite bool, err error))` in actions.go: it does the `shortcutsBlocked` guard, takes `a.navigator.Current()` on the main goroutine, runs `toggle` in a goroutine and reports back through `fyne.Do`. Keep the extra `metaOf(photo).Ratable` check inside `handleFavorite` before the call. In action_states.go, note that `photoStateChanged`'s `favorite` argument is only read when `ratingWritten` is true (`updateFavoriteButtonStates` re-reads the meta), so the `a.favoriteOf(photo)` that `handleColorToggle` passes today is dead: replace the three-argument method with `photoRatingChanged(photo model.Photo, favorite bool)` and `photoColorsChanged(photo model.Photo)` over a shared unexported core, and delete `favoriteOf`, whose only caller was that dead argument. The colour toggle then passes `false` for the favorite and never reads the navigator or the browser off the main goroutine.

steps.title: Remove the repeated nil-callback guards in internal/gui/ui
steps.details: Add `internal/gui/ui/callbacks.go` with `func call(fn func())` (calls fn when non-nil) and `func iconButton(label string, icon fyne.Resource, fn func()) *widget.Button` (a `widget.NewButtonWithIcon` whose handler is `func() { call(fn) }`). Apply to the 34 no-argument guards: `toolbar.go` (6 buttons in `build`), `contextmenu.go` (7 menu items — use `call` directly, `fyne.NewMenuItemWithIcon` has no button helper), `filebrowser.go` (the 10 buttons built in `build` and the two callback invocations in `SetPhotos`/`list.OnSelected`), `tags_dialog.go` (`OnClose`, `OnGenerate`, `OnCopyTitle`, `OnCopyKeywords`, `OnSaveJPEG`, `OnEscape` — leave the `d.saveJPEGBtn != nil` widget check alone), `gridviewer.go` (`OnPhotoTapped`, which takes an int argument, so only its guard is left in place), `viewer.go` (`OnTapped` uses `call`; `OnZoomChanged`/`OnSecondaryTapped` take arguments and stay as they are). No behaviour change and no new tests; `tags_dialog_test.go` already exercises those callbacks and must stay green.

steps.title: Factor the repeated refresh and button wiring in filebrowser.go
steps.details: Add `func (fb *FileBrowser) refreshRows()` for the `fb.data.applyFilter(); fb.updateBulkBarVisibility(); fb.list.Refresh()` triple repeated in `SetPhotos`, `RefreshFilter` (which additionally calls `updateFilterButtonStates`), `RemovePhoto` and `RemovePhotos`. Split `build()` (95 lines) into `buildList()`, `buildSortBar()`, `buildFilterBar()`, `buildBulkBar()` and the layout assembly; drive the four identical filter buttons from a table of `{icon fyne.Resource, callback func() func(), target **widget.Button}` or an equivalent small loop so the red/green/blue/favorite blocks stop being copy-paste. Simplify `HasActiveFilter` to `favorite || slices.Contains(slices.Collect(maps.Values(colors)), true)` or keep the loop if the linter's `modernize` rule prefers otherwise. `photolist_test.go` covers the data side and must stay green; no behaviour change.

steps.title: Move the row rendering out of filebrowser.go and test it
steps.details: Move `createItem`, `updateItem`, `browserItem`, `updateThumbnail`, `updateStar`, `updateColorDots`, `updateDateText`, the `favoriteMark`/`colorMark` constants, `favoriteColor` and the `thumbnailWidth`/`thumbnailHeight`/`dateFontSize` constants into a new `internal/gui/ui/browseritem.go`, leaving `filebrowser.go` with the widget wiring and the `photoList` delegation. Add `internal/gui/ui/browseritem_test.go` in the style of `photolist_test.go`/`tags_dialog_test.go`: `updateColorDots` shows one dot per active label in `colorOrder` and hides the leftovers when a row is reused for a photo with fewer colours; `updateDateText` clears the text for a zero date; `updateStar` hides and shows. These build `canvas.Text`/`fyne.Container` values directly and need no window.

steps.title: Share the inflight-load dance between Loader.Get and Loader.Preload
steps.details: `loadAsOwner` and the goroutine inside `Preload` both call `l.loadImage`, assign `w.img`/`w.size`/`w.err`, `close(w.done)` and then `addToCache` on success. Extract `func (l *Loader) runLoad(path string, size int, w *loadWaiter) (LoadedImage, error)` that performs the load and fills and closes the waiter, and let each caller keep its own caching rule — `Get` caches unconditionally, `Preload` only while its generation still matches — so the extraction cannot change what is cached after a folder switch. Also extract the `l.mu.Lock(); if _, ok := l.inflight[path]; ok {...}; w := &loadWaiter{done: ...}; l.inflight[path] = w; l.mu.Unlock()` registration both call sites repeat into a small `claimInflight`/`beginLoad` helper. `image_loader_test.go` covers generation bumps, byte budget and concurrent Get/Preload; extend it if any helper gains a case the existing tests do not reach.

steps.title: One sidecar-merge path in the imaging package
steps.details: `ExifService.GetStockInfo` (exif_tags.go) and `Provider.completeStock` (image_provider.go) both implement "when the photo has a RAW pair, read `model.SidecarPath(photo.RAWPath)` and `fillMissing(sidecar, info.Tags)`", with only their error handling differing (`GetStockInfo` joins the JPEG error, `completeStock` returns the info it already has). Add `func mergedWithSidecar(info StockInfo, photo model.Photo) (StockInfo, error)` in exif_tags.go that returns `info` untouched for a photo without a RAW pair and otherwise reads and folds in the sidecar, and call it from both places, keeping each caller's error wrapping at the call site. Existing coverage in `exif_tags_test.go` and `image_provider_test.go` (which exercises the cached/uncached and sidecar-wins cases) must stay green; add a case only if the helper introduces one they do not reach.

questions.question: The whole pass is meant to be behaviour-neutral - same dialogs, same shortcuts, same files written. Confirm that; in particular I am deliberately NOT giving the bulk dialogs the confirm-on-repeat behaviour that Delete and Copy have, because nothing binds a key to them. Assume behaviour-neutral unless told otherwise.

The imaging file names mislead more than the code does (`xmp.go` is really the XMP sidecar, `exif_tags.go` is the stock-info reader, `exif.go` is the ExifService). Do you want a pure-rename step (`xmp.go`->`sidecar.go`, `xmp_test.go`->`sidecar_test.go`, `exif_tags.go`->`stock_info.go`, `exif.go`->`exif_service.go`)? Assume no, since it costs blame history and would conflict with todos 2 and 3, unless you say yes.

`internal/gui/app` has no tests except `settings_test.go`, so steps 1-3 are verified by `go build`, `go tool golangci-lint run` and a manual run only. Is that acceptable, or should step 3 come with the first real test for that package (which needs a Fyne test window and stubs for scanner/colorService/exifService)? Assume acceptable as is.

Steps 1-3 rewrite `internal/gui/app/actions.go`, which todos 2 and 3 will also touch. Should this todo be done before those two to avoid conflicts? Assume yes (do this one first) unless the other work has already started.

risks: `internal/gui/app` is untested, so a slip in the confirm-dialog or toggle helpers (a missing `a.dialogs.closed()`, a guard dropped, work moved out of `fyne.Do`) would only show at runtime. Every helper must keep widget and navigator access on the main goroutine, per the fyne.Do rules in CLAUDE.md.

The `Loader` inflight/generation logic is subtle: `Get` caches whatever it loaded while `Preload` drops a load whose generation changed. Extracting a helper that unifies the caching rule would silently cache images from a folder the user has left.

Splitting `actions.go` and moving `filebrowser.go`'s row rendering makes merges with todos 2 (display tags on the photo) and 3 (background tag generation) harder if they are in flight at the same time.
`git mv`-style file moves lose blame continuity for large blocks; keeping the moves in their own commit (step 1, step 6) limits the damage.

Dropping `favoriteOf` and the favorite argument of `photoStateChanged` is only safe because `updateFavoriteButtonStates` re-reads the meta; if a future change makes the button state depend on the passed value, the colour path would need it back.

todos.description: Move all OS-dependent code into separate packages under internal
todos.context: Per-OS/build-tagged code should be pulled out of feature packages into dedicated single-purpose packages under internal, following the existing internal/core/clipboard and internal/core/proc pattern. The trigger is file_created_{darwin,windows,other}.go, added directly inside internal/core/imaging (fileCreated via syscall Birthtimespec / Win32FileAttributeData.CreationTime / ModTime), called from exif_tags.go. The other OS-split site is internal/gui/ui/maximize_{darwin,windows,unix}.go; internal/core/tags/claude_path.go switches on runtime.GOOS rather than build tags, and CLAUDE.md documents the package layout that must stay in sync.

plan.summary: Pull the remaining per-OS code out of the feature packages into dedicated single-purpose packages under `internal`, matching the `internal/core/clipboard` and `internal/core/proc` pattern. Three sites move: (1) `fileCreated` in `internal/core/imaging/file_created_{darwin,windows,other}.go` becomes a new `internal/core/filedate` package exporting `Created(path) time.Time`, with only the birth-time extraction kept behind build tags and the `os.Stat`/fallback logic shared; `imaging` (exif_tags.go `withFileDate`, plus the tests in exif_tags_test.go and orientation_test.go that call `fileCreated` directly) switches to it. (2) `internal/gui/ui/maximize_{darwin,windows,unix}.go` plus `maximize_darwin.m` move into a new `internal/gui/nativewin` package exporting `Maximize(fyne.Window)`; `screen.go`/`screen_test.go` must move with them because `maximize_unix.go` uses `screenLayout`/`maximizedContentSize`/`primaryVideoMode`, so `MonitorSize` becomes `nativewin.MonitorSize` and `internal/gui/app/app.go` is updated alongside `internal/gui/ui/window.go`. (3) `internal/core/tags/claude_path.go`, which branches on `runtime.GOOS` rather than build tags, moves wholesale into `internal/core/claudebin` as `Lookup`/`ErrNotFound`, keeping the runtime switch so both the Windows and the POSIX branches stay testable from any host. Each step also updates the package-layout tree in CLAUDE.md, which the project requires to stay in sync. Nothing new is imported into `internal/core` from Fyne, and all three steps keep `go build ./...`, the ubuntu CI build (which is what compiles the `!darwin && !windows` branches) and the mingw Windows cross-build working.

steps.title: Extract file creation time into internal/core/filedate
steps.details: Create `internal/core/filedate` with a shared `created.go`: `Created(path string) time.Time` does the `os.Stat`, returns the zero time on error, calls a per-OS `birthTime(info os.FileInfo) (time.Time, bool)` and falls back to `info.ModTime()` when it reports false. Add `birthtime_darwin.go` (`*syscall.Stat_t` -> `Birthtimespec`), `birthtime_windows.go` (`*syscall.Win32FileAttributeData` -> `CreationTime.Nanoseconds()`) and `birthtime_other.go` (`//go:build !darwin && !windows`, returns false). Keep the existing explanatory comments (the photo keeps the day it was taken, so it is dated by birth time and not by the last write) on `Created`/the per-OS files; the darwin and windows files need no build tag because the filename suffix already constrains them, exactly as today. Move `internal/core/imaging/file_created_test.go` to `internal/core/filedate/created_test.go` (package `filedate`, calling `Created`), keeping both cases (a freshly written file is dated now; a missing file has no date). Delete the three `internal/core/imaging/file_created_*.go` files, make `withFileDate` in `internal/core/imaging/exif_tags.go` call `filedate.Created`, and update the direct `fileCreated(path)` assertions in `internal/core/imaging/exif_tags_test.go` (~line 61) and `internal/core/imaging/orientation_test.go` (~lines 549, 565) to `filedate.Created(path)`. Add the `filedate/` line to the layout tree in CLAUDE.md. Verify with `go build ./...`, `go test ./internal/core/...` and a Windows cross-build (`CC=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc CGO_ENABLED=1 GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...`).

steps.title: Extract native window maximizing into internal/gui/nativewin
steps.details: Create `internal/gui/nativewin` and move `internal/gui/ui/maximize_darwin.go`, `maximize_darwin.m`, `maximize_windows.go` and `maximize_unix.go` into it unchanged except for the package clause, renaming the entry point `maximizeWindow` -> exported `Maximize(window fyne.Window)` in all three variants. The `.m` file must move together with the darwin `.go` file (it keeps its `//go:build darwin` line) or the cgo call to `maximizeNSWindow` fails to link. `screen.go` and `screen_test.go` move into the same package because `maximize_unix.go` depends on `screenLayout`, `screenMetrics`, `maximizedContentSize` and `primaryVideoMode`; `MonitorSize` stays exported and becomes `nativewin.MonitorSize`, everything else stays unexported. Update `internal/gui/ui/window.go` (`MainWindow.Maximize` calls `nativewin.Maximize(mw.window)`) and `internal/gui/app/app.go` (~line 118, the `fullImageSize` once-value now calls `nativewin.MonitorSize()` and imports `photo/internal/gui/nativewin`). `screen_test.go` moves as is apart from its package clause, so the `maximizedContentSize`/`centrableHeight` table tests keep running. Add the `nativewin/` entry under `gui/` in the CLAUDE.md layout tree. The `!windows && !darwin` variant is only compiled by the ubuntu CI job, so re-read `maximize_unix.go` after the move to confirm every symbol it uses now lives in the same package; check darwin locally with `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...`, and Windows with the mingw cross-build.

steps.title: Extract the claude CLI lookup into internal/core/claudebin
steps.details: Move `internal/core/tags/claude_path.go` to `internal/core/claudebin/lookup.go` (package `claudebin`), renaming `LookupClaude` -> `Lookup` and `ErrClaudeNotFound` -> `ErrNotFound` to avoid stutter and keeping the unexported `lookupClaude`, `claudeBinaries`, `claudeDirs`, `claudeCandidates`, `isExecutable` helpers and the `osWindows` constant. Keep the `runtime.GOOS` switches rather than splitting into build-tagged files, so the Windows candidate list stays covered by the tests on a macOS host; the OS knowledge is now confined to one single-purpose package. Move `claude_path_test.go` to `internal/core/claudebin/lookup_test.go` with the renames applied. Update `internal/core/tags/tagger.go` (`NewTagger` uses `claudebin.Lookup`, the `//nolint:gosec` comment on `exec.CommandContext` mentions the new name) and the call sites of the error: `internal/core/tags/tagger_test.go` (~lines 111, 117 use `claudebin.ErrNotFound`; ~line 338 loses the `osWindows` constant and must compare `runtime.GOOS` against the literal `"windows"`), `internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go` (~line 314) and `internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go` (~line 173), which now import `photo/internal/core/claudebin` instead of relying on `tags`. Add the `claudebin/` line to the CLAUDE.md layout tree. Run `go test ./...` and `go tool golangci-lint run`.

questions.question: Package naming: assume `internal/core/filedate` with `filedate.Created(path)`, `internal/gui/nativewin` with `nativewin.Maximize`/`nativewin.MonitorSize`, and `internal/core/claudebin` with `claudebin.Lookup`/`claudebin.ErrNotFound` unless you prefer other names (affects all three steps).

Step 1 restructures `fileCreated` into a shared `Created` plus a per-OS `birthTime(info)` instead of three near-identical copies of the stat-and-fallback code. Assume yes; say so if you want a literal 1:1 move of the three files.

Step 2 moves `screen.go`/`screen_test.go` out of `internal/gui/ui` as well (they are not OS-specific but `maximize_unix.go` needs them), so `ui.MonitorSize` becomes `nativewin.MonitorSize` and `internal/gui/app/app.go` changes. Assume yes; the alternative is keeping a one-line `ui.MonitorSize` wrapper so `app.go` is untouched.

Step 3 keeps `runtime.GOOS` branching inside the new `claudebin` package rather than converting it to `_windows.go`/`_other.go` files, because build tags would make the Windows path untestable on the dev machine and CI (both non-Windows). Assume yes; say so if you want build-tagged files with per-OS tests like `internal/core/proc`.

risks: The darwin maximize is cgo: `maximize_darwin.m` must move together with `maximize_darwin.go` (and keep its `//go:build darwin` line), otherwise the macOS build fails to link `maximizeNSWindow`.

The `!darwin && !windows` variants (`birthtime_other.go`, `maximize_unix.go`) are not compiled on the developer's macOS host; only the ubuntu CI job builds them, so a missed symbol in the moved `maximize_unix.go` will only surface in CI.

The Windows-only files (`birthtime_windows.go`, `maximize_windows.go`) likewise only compile under `GOOS=windows`; the mingw cross-build must be run for each step, and `fyne package --release --os windows` bumps the build number in FyneApp.toml as a side effect, so prefer plain `GOOS=windows go build ./...` for verification.

Renaming `ErrClaudeNotFound` -> `claudebin.ErrNotFound` touches the GUI (`tags_dialog.go`); the `errors.Is` check must keep pointing at the same sentinel or the "claude CLI not found" branch of the tags dialog silently stops matching.
`tagger_test.go` borrows the `osWindows` constant from `claude_path.go`; if the constant leaves the package without that test being updated, the `tags` package stops compiling.
CLAUDE.md documents the package layout and is loaded as project context; leaving it stale is a real (if non-breaking) regression, so each step should update the tree it changes.
